questions.prompt: Which machine fits each job best?
questions.explain: Known rule: a program. Narrow, validated task with no known rule: a trained model. Open-ended draft you can check: an LLM.

items.text: Count sequences in a FASTA file
items.misconception: The rule is exact and known, so use a program. An LLM may miscount.

items.text: Predict gene locations in a new bacterial genome
items.misconception: That is a narrow task with validated tools trained for it.

items.text: Draft a first version of a plotting script you will test
items.misconception: Open-ended drafting that you can run and verify suits an LLM.

items.text: Convert a GFF file to BED with a fixed rule
items.misconception: A fixed conversion rule is exactly what a script is for.
Explaining text is a strength, and you can check the explanation by trying it.

questions.prompt: You put an LLM call inside a pipeline step that cleans species names. What must you do that you would not for a plain script?
questions.explain: The step is no longer deterministic, so you need to check outputs and record which model produced them.

options.text: Validate outputs and record the model and version, since runs can differ
Write one unit test once, since the function will behave the same every time
options.misconception: An LLM call can return different text each time and can be wrong, so one test proves little.

options.text: Run it once, cache the result for reuse, and skip checking it afterwards
options.misconception: Caching a wrong answer preserves the error. Validate it first.

questions.prompt: A published trained model predicts protein domains with a measured accuracy on a benchmark. When is it reasonable to trust it?
questions.explain: A trained model's accuracy applies to the kind of data it was validated on.

options.text: On data similar to what it was validated on, with spot-checks
On any organism, since the benchmark score already covers them
options.misconception: Accuracy does not transfer automatically to very different data.

options.text: Only if an LLM independently reaches the same answer
options.misconception: An LLM agreeing is not validation.

questions.prompt: A rule is exact and known (rename columns by a fixed mapping). Which is best?
questions.explain: When you know the rule, writing it down gives a result you can read and rerun.

options.text: A short script, perhaps LLM-drafted and then tested
Paste the table into a chat and ask it to rename the columns
options.misconception: That is slow, unrepeatable and might alter values silently.

options.text: Train a small model on examples of old and new names
options.misconception: Training is overkill for a rule you can write in one line.
